settings.heroTitle: Adventure, friendship and the outdoors, on the edge of the Burren.
settings.heroLede: 7th Clare Scout Group in Ballyvaughan welcomes young people from 6 to 17. We camp, hike, build, cook, paddle and learn to look after each other and the wild places around us.
settings.about:
We're a volunteer-run Scout Group based in Ballyvaughan, County Clare, part of Scouting Ireland. Our programme is built around the Burren: limestone hills, the Atlantic on our doorstep, caves, green roads and dark skies.

Young people plan their own adventures with the support of trained adult leaders, gaining skills, confidence and a lasting love of the outdoors along the way.

kits.title: Sionnach Adventure
kits.event: Two nights under canvas in the mountains, patrols of four plus one leader, Friday night to Sunday
kits.summary: You carry everything for two nights on the hill: tent, food, water, cooking gear and clothes. One rucksack only (65 to 70 litres is plenty), nothing carried in your hands, and no day bags. Staff check gear at Friday check-in and anyone missing essentials is sent home, so pack it yourself and pack it at the meeting the week before.

docs.title: Sionnach Adventure: Fail to Prepare, Prepare to Fail (PDF)
docs.note: The official preparation guide. Read it with your patrol before packing night.

docs.title: sionnach.org
docs.note: Full kit list and a sample programme for the three meetings before a Sionnach.

tips: Packing night: bring your packed rucksack to the meeting the week before. Empty it, repack it with the patrol, add the shared troop kit, then get a leader to adjust the straps. Weight on the hips, not the shoulders, and nothing swinging.
Line the rucksack with a heavy-duty plastic bag (a compost or fertiliser bag is ideal) and put sleeping bag and spare clothes in their own dry bags inside. Double waterproofing is the rule.

Heavy things close to your back, middle to bottom. Sleeping bag at the bottom in a compression sack, mat on top. Waterproofs, head torch, map, compass, snacks and water go in the lid or side pockets: Friday night arrival is dark and chaotic.
Everything must fit inside the bag except the roll mat and tent poles. Gear hanging off the outside wastes energy and gets wet.

Practise before you go: taking and walking on a bearing, adding magnetic variation, pacing 100 m, and writing a route card from the map extract the coordinator emails out. Do not write or draw on your map.
Friday: eat dinner before you leave or on the way. A light supper (biscuits, a hot dog) is all you'll cook on arrival. Get to sleep; Saturday is long.

Saturday: leaders' meeting at about 9 am, then walk to High Camp. Pitch away from hollows and water channels, peg out fully and use every guy line even if the weather looks fine. Leave gear in a dry bag, don't lay out bedding yet.

From High Camp you head out for the summit or horseshoe loop with just a bag, lunch, first aid kit, storm shelter, Trangia, torch and one well-protected sleeping bag. Only stop for lunch at a checkpoint.
Boil water from the stream for dinner, put warm layers on before it gets cold and dark, and take every scrap of rubbish home. Leave no trace.

Sunday: Scouts' Own at High Camp, badges, then walk out. Leave a full change of clothes in the car for the drive home. Small car parks mean you may be blocked in for a while, so tell whoever is collecting you.

kits.title: Mountain Pursuit Challenge (MPC)
kits.event: Weekend navigation challenge, teams of four plus a leader observer, Friday night to Sunday
kits.summary: MPC is navigation day and night through the mountains, fully self-sufficient. You carry everything: two nights of camping, food, water and cooking gear, and you will be walking in the dark on Friday night. The kit is the same as a Sionnach with more emphasis on light, torches, warm layers and being able to find things in your bag without unpacking it.
tips: Every item has a place in your bag and you know where it is with your eyes closed. Night navigation is where badly packed bags fall apart.
Two light sources per person: a good head torch on your head and a small backup torch in your pocket. Fresh batteries in both, spares in a ziplock.
Weight matters more on MPC than on any other event. Aim for a rucksack that is no more than a quarter of your body weight once shared kit is divided out.
You will camp late on Friday night. Have your sleeping clothes, mat and bag packed together at the top of the main compartment so camp takes ten minutes, not forty.
Practice route cards, pacing 100 metres, walking on a bearing and adding magnetic variation before you go. The observer cannot help you navigate.

kits.title: One night camping
kits.event: A single night under canvas, usually a Friday or Saturday, all sections
kits.summary: One night out is the first taste of camping for Beavers and Cubs and a regular thing for Scouts. Tents and cooking gear are shared, so this is personal kit only. Pack it in one bag with your child, so they know where everything is.
tips: Pack with your child, not for them. Talk through where the torch is, where the warm layer is, where the spare socks are.
Everything in the bag goes inside a bin bag or dry bag first. Tents leak, bags get left in wet grass.
Layers beat one big coat: base layer, fleece, jacket. Nights are cold even in June.
Write your child's name on the bag and on the sleeping bag.

kits.title: Multi-day standing camp
kits.event: Three nights or more on one site: summer camp, county camp, jamborees
kits.summary: A standing camp is camping in one place for several days with a full programme: activities, cooking in patrols, and usually a day out. Bags come by car so weight matters less, but everything still has to survive rain, mud and being lived out of for a week. One big bag, plus a small day bag for activities.

badges.intro: Every young person works through the same nine Adventure Skills, from stage 1 to stage 9, whichever section they are in. You start at stage 1 no matter your age, keep the highest stage badge you have earned on your sleeve, and replace it when you move up. Most Scouts settle on two or three skills they really enjoy rather than trying all nine.
badges.stages: As a rough guide, Beavers usually reach stages 1 to 2, Cubs stages 2 to 4, Scouts stages 3 to 6 and Ventures stages 5 to 9, but the stages are not tied to sections and a keen Cub can be ahead of a new Scout.
